# India Extends Cotton Import Duty Exemption Until December 31 to Lower Textile Costs

India has extended its exemption on cotton import duties, keeping the waiver in place until December 31. The measure is designed to curb expenses across the country's textile sector, according to a report by The Economic Times.

Under this decision, inbound shipments of cotton will continue to enter India without the standard customs duties applied. The policy prolongation ensures that the tariff relief remains active through the end of the calendar year.

The primary objective behind stretching the exemption period is to provide financial relief to textile producers. By removing import taxes on raw cotton, authorities aim to lower input costs and reduce the broader production expenses that businesses in the textile supply chain are currently facing.

Raw cotton serves as a critical basic material for yarn manufacturers, garment makers, and mills. The continued exemption allows these operations to procure overseas cotton supplies without having to absorb extra tariff-related overhead.

With the December 31 deadline now established, industry participants have a clear timeframe for duty-free cotton imports. The extended window gives domestic firms continued flexibility in sourcing their material needs from international markets under the relaxed tariff terms.

This ongoing waiver represents a targeted effort to address cost pressures within India's textile manufacturing industry, maintaining duty-free access for imported cotton through the final month of the year.
